title: Nav Chorus: workspace-aware sidebar & route stitching
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design a workspace-aware sidebar that dynamically stitches routes and surfaces contextual dashboard and rollout controls. Focus: reduce cognitive load when switching workspaces, surface cost quick-actions and rollout toggles, and provide a fast keyboard-first path for power users while preserving clarity for new users. Deliverables: low/hi-fi prototypes, interaction spec, accessibility checklist, and handoff tokens for engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Sidebar displays workspace context (name + active project) and adjusts primary route order based on recent user activity.
Cost lens and rollout quick-actions are reachable within two clicks or a single keyboard chord from any route.
Workspace switcher preserves in-flight route intent (route stitching) so dashboards/rollouts open in the same relative panel after switch.
Prototype passes internal accessibility checklist (keyboard nav, focus states, ARIA labels) and a 4:1 contrast target for critical controls.
Design tokens and spacing map provided to engineering; interactions documented with 6 example flows and edge cases.
Telemetry hooks defined for measuring 'switch+open' task success rate and average time-to-first-interaction for cost views.
Engineering sign-off received on feasibility of persistent route intent and progressive enhancement for small screens.
comments: 2025-02-19 - Maya Patel: Initial concept review posted. Emphasis on two patterns: (A) lightweight contextual rail that reorders and (B) full-expanded hub with micro-lenses. Attached early sketches and flow diagrams.

2025-02-24 - Arjun Shah (Engineering): Raised complexity concern around preserving KV cache state across workspace switch. Suggested we consider 'intent tokens' that map to safe fallbacks (dashboard->summary view) if model/context mismatch.

2025-02-25 - Priya Kaur (PM): Likes the route stitching idea for admin flows. Requested measurable goals: reduce workspace-switch-to-dashboard time from baseline and lower accidental workspace context loss incidents.
2025-03-01 - Accessibility review (Riley Chen): Noted focus ring/color contrast fixes; requested ARIA labels for nested quick actions and clear skip links for keyboard users.

2025-03-03 - Design critique: Lean toward the rail-first pattern for small screens; full hub reserved for large displays. Trade-off: slightly more discovery friction for power users vs simpler default for newcomers.
2025-03-05 - Riley Chen: Updated prototype (Figma v1.3) with keyboard chord (G then W) to open workspace quick-jump and preserved intent when switching. Ready for engineering feasibility review.
